name: Apache Pulsar
summary: A distributed messaging and streaming platform that separates stateless broker serving and dispatch from BookKeeper message storage and metadata-store coordination.

features.name: Stateless broker serving and dispatch
features.description: Pulsar brokers expose administrative and topic-lookup HTTP APIs, accept producer and consumer connections, and dispatch data over the binary protocol. The official architecture describes brokers as stateless and assigns each topic to one broker at a time.
benefits: Separates client serving and dispatch from persistent message storage
Allows broker capacity and ownership to be managed independently of stored ledgers
Supports service discovery and redirection to the topic owner
costs: Topic ownership and load balancing require coordination
Broker failure can interrupt serving even when storage remains available
A stateless serving layer does not remove network and metadata dependencies

features.name: Managed ledgers with independent cursors
features.description: Pulsar models a topic's storage as a managed ledger built from multiple BookKeeper ledgers. The managed-ledger abstraction has a single appending writer and multiple consuming cursors, each with its own position; rollover permits failed ledgers to be replaced and consumed ledgers to be deleted.
benefits: Provides sequential append behavior with independent subscription progress
Allows ledger rollover after failures or consumption progress
Scales topic storage across multiple bookies and ledgers
costs: Cursor and ledger lifecycle add metadata and recovery state
A single-writer abstraction constrains append ownership
Deleting old ledgers depends on all relevant cursors progressing

features.name: Replicated BookKeeper persistence
features.description: Pulsar uses Apache BookKeeper bookies for persistent message storage. BookKeeper ledgers replicate entries across bookies, recover the last committed entry after failure, and provide consistent reads of a recovered ledger.
benefits: Distributes capacity and I/O across storage nodes
Retains replicated entries across bookie failures
Provides a clear recovery boundary for an append log
costs: Replication adds storage and network cost
Recovery and ledger fencing complicate the write lifecycle
Durability depends on deployment and ensemble configuration

features.name: Metadata-store and message-store separation
features.description: Pulsar separates message data in BookKeeper from cluster and instance metadata in a metadata store. The official architecture assigns topic metadata, ownership, configuration, and coordination responsibilities to these metadata-store layers.
benefits: Separates control-plane metadata from the message data path
Permits supported metadata backends to be selected for deployment needs
Makes cluster-level and instance-wide coordination explicit
costs: Operations require both metadata and storage services
Metadata-store availability affects ownership and coordination
Multiple scopes of metadata increase deployment complexity

mathematical_views.question: How are topic-serving brokers related to the persistent ledgers and metadata that back them?
assumptions: A topic has one active serving broker in the modeled interval
A managed ledger is represented by an ordered family of BookKeeper ledgers
Metadata edges describe coordination and ownership rather than message payload flow

mathematical_views.question: When can a topic's segmented log advance, recover, and reclaim storage while preserving subscription positions?
assumptions: Each segment has one writer until it is closed or fenced
Cursors identify the positions required by subscriptions
Ledger recovery establishes a committed prefix before readers resume

benefits: Independent serving scale and storage placement
costs: Ownership, lookup, and redirection require coordination

benefits: Efficient append with independent subscription progress
costs: Segment and cursor cleanup requires lifecycle tracking
